findings.title: Imported feed/remote HTML is stored and rendered without sanitization
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import creates posts with cook_method raw_html (and the update path at line 36 does the same), and Post#cook returns raw verbatim for such posts, so cooked == raw. Neither PollFeed content nor the absolutize_urls step sanitizes the HTML: script tags, event-handler attributes (e.g. ), javascript: URLs etc. from an RSS/Atom feed item survive into the stored post and are output with `raw post.cooked` in the embed view and in normal topic rendering. Anyone who can influence a polled feed (or a page fetched via import_remote, where the PollFeed path bypasses Readability's tag whitelist entirely) gets stored XSS in the browsers of forum visitors and admins.

findings.title: request.referer is interpolated unescaped into a script and misused as postMessage targetOrigin
findings.body: The layout embeds '<%= request.referer %>' directly inside a single-quoted JavaScript string with no escaping (no j/escape_javascript or JSON encoding). A referer containing a single quote or </script> breaks out of the string and executes attacker script in the embed page on the Discourse origin. Independently, postMessage's targetOrigin must be an origin (scheme://host:port), but a full referer URL including path is passed, so browsers will not deliver the discourse-resize message and iframe resizing silently never works.

findings.title: postMessage origin check is an inverted substring test
findings.body: The handler accepts a message when `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is false, i.e. when e.origin appears anywhere as a substring of discourseUrl, instead of comparing e.origin for equality with the Discourse origin. Short or partial origins that happen to be substrings of the configured URL (for example a bare scheme or host fragment) are accepted, letting pages from unintended origins drive the discourse-resize handling. The check should parse discourseUrl to its origin and require strict equality.

findings.title: import_remote fetches an attacker-influenced URL with open() and no SSRF safeguards
findings.body: TopicRetriever only compares URI(embed_url).host to embeddable_host, then TopicEmbed.import_remote does open(url).read with no timeout, size limit, or redirect control. open-uri follows redirects, so a URL on the allowed host that redirects to an internal address (e.g. 169.254.169.254 or localhost admin endpoints) bypasses the host check and the server fetches internal content (SSRF); a slow or huge response also ties up the Sidekiq worker indefinitely. Fetching should re-validate the host after redirects, block private/link-local addresses, and set open/read timeouts and a size cap.

findings.title: poll_feed crashes on feed items without content (and on Ruby < 2.1)
findings.body: CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) raises NoMethodError whenever an RSS/Atom item has no content element (SimpleRSS returns nil for missing fields, common for summary-only feeds), and String#scrub does not exist on the Ruby 1.9/2.0 runtimes this codebase targets. Because there is no per-item rescue, one such item aborts the whole hourly poll mid-loop: remaining items are never imported and the job fails on every run. The title at line 36 can likewise be nil. Guard nil fields and isolate failures per item.

findings.title: Every request for an unknown embed_url enqueues a new retrieve job
findings.body: When no TopicEmbed exists, each GET /embed/best enqueues another Jobs::RetrieveTopic, and the loading page auto-reloads every 30 seconds, so a single embedded page (or a bot hitting the endpoint with rotating embed_url values, needing only a matching Referer) can flood Sidekiq with jobs and outbound fetches. The 60-second throttle lives inside TopicRetriever at job-execution time, so it does not stop unbounded enqueueing. Deduplicate/throttle at enqueue time (e.g. a redis setnx keyed by embed_url before Jobs.enqueue).

findings.title: Check-then-create race on embed_url despite the unique index
findings.body: import does TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first and only creates the embed inside the transaction when blank, but topic_embeds has a unique index on embed_url. Two concurrent executions (hourly PollFeed overlapping a RetrieveTopic job for the same URL, or two retrieve jobs) can both see no embed, both create a topic/post via PostCreator, and then one raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique on TopicEmbed.create!, rolling back and failing the job after side effects such as job enqueues from post creation. The create path needs to rescue RecordNotUnique and reload the winning embed, or serialize import per URL.

findings.title: Embed controller spec expects synchronous TopicRetriever but controller enqueues a job
findings.body: The 'tells the topic retriever to work' example stubs TopicRetriever.new and expects retrieve to be called, but EmbedController#best never references TopicRetriever; it calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...). As written the mocha expectation is never satisfied and this example fails, so the PR's own test suite is red and the actual enqueued-args behaviour (user_id, embed_url) is untested. Update the spec to expect Jobs.enqueue with :retrieve_topic and the right arguments.
